title: The contract meeting after the pear harvest
public_context: Harvest contracts often combine individual piece rates with shared quality or delivery conditions. A hearing record can reveal how grades are assigned, which weather events affect guaranteed pay, and how a crew resolves a disputed lot. Different orchards set different terms, so the minutes should be read as one association's agreement.
source_title: Hill Ladder growers' contract hearing minutes
source_text:
The Hill Ladder growers met on 12 August to settle the pear-picking account after three crews challenged the grade summary. Their contract paid each picker by accepted crate and added a crew bonus if every scheduled row was cleared before the packing shed's Friday noon cutoff. A separate base payment covered hours worked during a weather stop. The growers brought the weighing slips and the graders' marked cards to the meeting.

The dispute concerned six crates from the western row. The picker captain said the pears had been placed in the wrong grade after a bruised branch fell during loading. The shed grader showed that the crate cards had been marked before the cart left the row, and the captain agreed that the bruises were visible then. The committee kept four crates in the lower grade and moved two to the market grade after checking the stored fruit. The revised decision was written on both the crew sheet and the shed copy.

A storm stopped work at 2:40 on Wednesday. The crews moved the remaining crates beneath the packing awning, and the supervisor recorded the stop time for the base payment. The contract did not count a weather-stopped row as cleared for the Friday bonus, even if its fruit had already been picked. The growers voted to honor the base payment and waive the cutoff for one crew whose scheduled row was inaccessible after a fallen limb blocked the lane. No other crew received a cutoff waiver.

By Friday noon, the other two crews had cleared their assigned rows. The blocked crew's lane remained inaccessible until a county crew removed the fallen limb Friday afternoon; that crew cleared its row after work resumed that evening. The shed clerk reconciled each accepted crate with a weighing slip, and the treasurer posted piece pay before calculating the collective bonus. The minutes state that all three crews received the bonus, including the crew whose cutoff was waived. The growers asked the supervisor to photograph future lane obstructions before moving them, so a later waiver would have a dated record.

The meeting closed with a unanimous vote to keep the grade cards attached to the weekly pay sheet. The minutes report no further challenge to the six crates. The secretary filed the signed vote beside the grade cards before the pay sheets were sent to the treasurer.

consistency_questions.question: How did the grade appeal differ from the weather-related bonus exception?
consistency_questions.reference_answer: The six-crate appeal changed the grade of two crates after inspection. Separately, the contract excluded weather-stopped rows from cutoff clearance, but the growers waived that deadline for the limb-blocked crew, and all three crews ultimately received the bonus.

consistency_questions.question: Which records linked fruit acceptance, pay, and later review?
consistency_questions.reference_answer: Accepted crates were reconciled to weighing slips before piece pay and the collective bonus were calculated; grade cards were attached to the weekly pay sheet for review.
